title: Forgotten Land
synopsis: Set to Benjamin Britten's Sinfonia da Requiem, the ballet evokes the relentless power of the ocean and the emotional erosion of memory and loss. Dancers move against an expansive backdrop featuring a seascape by artist Edvard Munch, depicting couples in states of passionate attachment, separation, and mourning.
history_and_evolution: Commissioned by the Stuttgart Ballet, Kylián was inspired by Munch's painting *Women on the Beach*. The work showcases his distinctive lyrical fluidity combined with themes of existential transience.

historical_performances.relevance: Marked a major exploration of psychological depth and tragic resonance in Kylián's oeuvre.

title: Bella Figura
synopsis: A surreal contemporary masterpiece performed on a stage framed by massive burning candles and mobile sliding walls. Dancers perform in various stages of undress, exploring the illusion of performance, physical vanity, dreams, and the facades ('bella figura') humans project to society.
history_and_evolution: One of Kylián's most celebrated black-and-white theater pieces for Nederlands Dans Theater, utilizing Baroque music juxtaposed with striking theatrical lighting and stark spatial geometry.

historical_performances.relevance: Redefined theatrical minimalism and postmodern European dance dramaturgy.

title: Petit Mort
synopsis: Created for the Mozart Bicentennial, six men and six women execute precise, sensual choreography with six fencing foils, black ball gowns, and rolling Elizabethan dress stands, symbolizing vulnerability, interpersonal tension, and mortality ('little death').
history_and_evolution: Became an international repertory favorite due to its brilliant integration of Mozart's slow piano concertos with sharp martial props and classical line deconstruction.
key_variations: Dresses on Wheels Pas de Deux

historical_performances.relevance: Became one of the most widely performed contemporary ballet works worldwide.

title: Symphony of Psalms
synopsis: Set to Stravinsky's choral masterpiece, the choreography explores spiritual devotion, collective human suffering, and resurrection. Dancers use floor-based contractions and expansive arm gestures that mirror the monumental choral text.
history_and_evolution: Kylián's breakthrough international success that established his affinity for religious and ritualistic themes mapped onto modern neoclassical technique.

historical_performances.relevance: Propelled Kylián into global choreographic prominence.

title: The Concert (or The Perils of Everybody)
premiere_location: New York City Center, New York
synopsis: A hilarious comedic ballet depicting various eccentric audience members sitting at a piano recital daydreaming. Fantasies range from romantic entanglements and murderous urges to surreal dream sequences where dancers wear butterfly lampshades on their heads.
history_and_evolution: Jerome Robbins's masterwork of physical comedy and musical parody, demonstrating that classical ballet dancers can be brilliant satirical actors.

historical_performances.relevance: Set the gold standard for balletic comedy and musical character satire.

title: Dances at a Gathering
premiere_location: New York State Theater, New York
synopsis: An abstract masterpiece for ten dancers set to a collection of Chopin piano pieces. Without a plot, it explores complex nuances of friendship, flirtation, solitude, and community through subtle folk-infused movements under an open sky backdrop.
history_and_evolution: Created for New York City Ballet to honor Chopin's music, it is celebrated for its natural, unpretentious elegance and deep emotional resonance.
characters: Five Men and Five Women (Identified by costume colors)

historical_performances.relevance: Celebrated as one of the greatest plotless chamber ballets of the 20th century.

title: The Dybbuk
premiere_location: New York State Theater, New York
synopsis: Act I: Two friends vow that if they have children of opposite sexes, they will marry. Years later, one friend breaks the pact, leading to tragedy when the son dies. Act II: The deceased youth's spirit returns as a dybbuk, possessing his beloved on her wedding day before an exorcism forces him out, leaving her dead of a broken heart.
history_and_evolution: Based on S. Ansky's mystical Yiddish play. It marked the final major collaboration between Leonard Bernstein and Jerome Robbins, dealing with dark supernatural themes.

historical_performances.relevance: Explored mystic Jewish folklore through rigorous modern neoclassical choreography.

title: The Cage
premiere_location: New York City Center, New York
synopsis: Set in an insect-like matriarchal society, a Queen Queen instructs a newly born Novice insect how to kill and feed on intruder males, until the Novice falls in love with an intruder and is ultimately destroyed by her own swarm for failing to complete her mission.
history_and_evolution: Stravinsky's String Concerto in D provided the framework for Robbins's visceral, predatory choreography examining female aggression and primitive survival instincts.

historical_performances.relevance: Pioneered predatory animalistic movement styles within classical modern ballet.

title: Afternoon of a Faun
premiere_location: New York City Center, New York
synopsis: Set in a modern ballet studio with a large practice mirror facing the audience, a young male dancer stretches lazily. A female dancer enters, they share a brief, intensely focused pas de deux mirrored reflection, and she departs, leaving him alone with his reflection.
history_and_evolution: Robbins reimagined Nijinsky's legendary 1912 scandalous faun concept into a contemporary American ballet studio setting, exploring narcissism and erotic tension under studio lights.

historical_performances.relevance: Reinterpreted a modernist historical scandal into a sleek mid-century American context.

multimedia.youtube_query: Afternoon of a Faun Jerome Robbins NYCB

title: Glass Pieces
premiere_location: New York State Theater, New York
synopsis: A three-movement minimalist abstract ballet set to music by Philip Glass. The first movement features pulsing geometric lines of marching dancers; the second showcases a lyrical hypnotic couple floating across urban chaos; the third explodes into high-energy rhythmic ensemble dynamics.
history_and_evolution: Robbins's triumphant engagement with minimalist music, bridging classical vocabulary with urban pulsation and contemporary minimalism.

historical_performances.relevance: Demonstrated the seamless synergy between classical technique and minimalist music.

title: Liebeslieder Walzer
premiere_location: New York City Center, New York
synopsis: Act I: Four couples dance intimate, flowing waltzes in a formal drawing room setting to live onstage vocalists and piano. Act II: The setting shifts to a dreamlike ethereal mirror-lined pavilion where dancers shed their ballroom formality into pure romantic abstraction.
history_and_evolution: A masterwork of social dance elevated to high art, exploring subtle psychological currents and deep romantic longing through the Viennese waltz form.

historical_performances.relevance: Elevated the traditional social waltz into a masterpiece of psychological neoclassical chamber art.

title: Union Jack
premiere_location: New York State Theater, New York
synopsis: A grand patriotic and folkloric celebration of British naval and military history divided into three sections: Navy sailors performing crisp hornpipes, Scottish Highlanders dancing in kilts and tartans, and a dazzling finale featuring costumed pearly kings and queens.
history_and_evolution: Created for the US Bicentennial celebration as a tribute to British dance traditions, showcasing Balanchine's versatility in handling folk idiom with academic precision.

historical_performances.relevance: Showcased Balanchine's mastery of stylized folk and national character dance.

title: Brahms-Schoenberg Quartetni
premiere_location: New York State Theater, New York
synopsis: A grand four-movement neoclassical epic. Movement I and II are lush romantic German waltzes; Movement III is a Hungarian-flavored gypsy dance; Movement IV is an explosive, virtuosic display of grand allegro and royal splendor.
history_and_evolution: Balanchine utilized Schoenberg's rich, massive orchestration of Brahms's Piano Quartet in G minor to create a lavish tribute to 19th-century imperial style.

historical_performances.relevance: Bridged romantic Brahms melodies with Schoenberg's orchestral scale in grand neoclassical fashion.

title: Stravinsky Violin Concertoni
premiere_location: New York State Theater, New York
synopsis: An abstract neoclassical ballet structured in four parts (Toccata, two Arias, and a Capriccio). The choreography matches Stravinsky's biting neoclassical score with sharp torso contractions, complex footwork, and playful dynamic geometry.
history_and_evolution: Created for the 1972 Stravinsky Festival by New York City Ballet, it stands as one of Balanchine's most celebrated geometric collaborations with the composer.

historical_performances.relevance: Premiered during the historic Stravinsky Festival, cementing a legendary musical alliance.

title: Divertimento No. 15ni
synopsis: A pure neoclassical masterpiece for eight principal dancers and an ensemble set to Mozart's sparkling divertimento. The work highlights supreme technical clarity, rapid footwork, and elegant aristocratic poise without any narrative plot.
history_and_evolution: Created for the American Shakespeare Festival, it is widely considered the ultimate test of pure academic classicism and ballerina transparency in the Balanchine repertory.
characters: Five Ballerinas, Three Cavaliers, and Ensemble

historical_performances.relevance: Established the ultimate benchmark for pure classical academic transparency and phrasing.
